summary: Dublin is a vibrant capital city blending medieval history with modern Irish culture, featuring world-class museums, literary heritage, and a thriving pub scene. The Liffey River winds through Georgian architecture and bustling neighborhoods filled with street art, craft breweries, and warm-hearted locals.

restaurants.mustTry: Battered cod and chips with mushy peas

restaurants.name: The Winding Stair

restaurants.name: Bunsen

activities.name: Guinness Storehouse
activities.description: Seven-story interactive museum dedicated to Ireland's most famous beer, featuring brewing history, tasting experiences, and 360-degree city views from the Gravity Bar.

activities.name: Trinity College Library & Book of Kells
activities.description: Visit one of the world's oldest libraries housing the illuminated medieval manuscript, the Book of Kells, plus stunning Long Room with 200,000+ volumes.

activities.name: Temple Bar Pub Crawl
activities.description: Explore Dublin's most historic quarter filled with traditional pubs offering live Irish music, craft beers, and authentic social atmosphere.

activities.name: Dublin Castle Tour
activities.description: Step back 800 years exploring the seat of Irish power, featuring medieval towers, state rooms, and underground passages.

activities.name: Howth Cliff Walk
activities.description: Stunning 6km coastal cliff walk north of Dublin offering panoramic sea views, seaside villages, and diverse seabird watching opportunities.

activities.name: National Museum of Ireland
activities.description: World-class museum spanning prehistoric Irish artifacts to natural history, with free admission to permanent collections.

activities.name: Phoenix Park Bike Ride
activities.description: Europe's largest urban park offering 11 sq km of green space, grazing deer herds, monuments, and peaceful cycling routes.

activities.name: Ha'penny Bridge & Liffey River Walk
activities.description: Iconic cast-iron bridge offering picturesque photo opportunities and scenic riverside walks through Dublin's historic heart.

activities.name: Christ Church Cathedral
activities.description: Medieval cathedral dating to 1028 featuring original stonework, the Crypt, and views of Dublin from the tower.

activities.name: Irish Whiskey Museum
activities.description: Interactive museum tracing Irish whiskey history with distillery tours, tastings, and hands-on barrel experiments.

activities.name: Grafton Street & Shopping District
activities.description: Vibrant pedestrian shopping street filled with street performers, boutiques, historic architecture, and bustling cafe culture.

activities.name: Dail Eireann Parliament Tour
activities.description: Tour the Irish Parliament building in Leinster House with free guided visits exploring the legislative chambers and historic rooms.

spots.name: Ha'penny Bridge at Dawn

spots.name: Temple Bar District Streets
spots.description: Narrow cobblestone streets with colorful facades, hanging flower baskets, and atmospheric alleyways ideal for street photography.

spots.name: Christ Church Cathedral Interior

spots.name: Dublin Castle Courtyard

spots.name: Howth Cliffs Seascape

spots.name: Phoenix Park Deer & Trees

spots.name: Temple Bar at Night

spots.name: Liffey Quays at Sunset

spots.name: Grafton Street Crowds

spots.bestTime: Afternoon and evening when street is busy

spots.name: Dublin Library Long Room

lensRecommendations: 16-35mm wide-angle for architectural and landscape shots of bridges and cityscapes
50mm prime for street photography and intimate temple bar scenes
70-200mm telephoto for wildlife at Phoenix Park and coastal seabird photography
14mm ultra-wide for dramatic interior shots of cathedrals and library vaults
photography.goldenHourNotes: Dublin's golden hour is particularly magical during spring and summer (May-August) when the sun sets around 9-10 PM, providing extended photography windows. The Liffey and historic facades glow warm amber during this time. Winter golden hours are shorter but offer dramatic cloud formations and moody light perfect for atmospheric street photography.

weather.seasonality: Dublin experiences mild, rainy weather year-round with the warmest months June-August averaging 20-22°C. Late spring (May) and early autumn (September) offer the best combination of comfortable temperatures and lower rainfall, though rain remains frequent throughout the year.
weather.summary: Dublin's maritime climate brings frequent rain and overcast skies, particularly October-March, with temperatures rarely dropping below freezing or exceeding 23°C. Pack waterproof layers year-round; summer visitors should expect cooler conditions than continental Europe at similar latitudes.

hotels.name: Hostel Dublin City Center
